name: Miaplacidus
description: A subgiant of type A1 IV 34.7 parsecs away, 5.9 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Narrabri intensity interferometer.

paper.credit: Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417

radius.source: Computed here, not printed by a paper: 5.93 +/- 0.26 solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.59 +/- 0.07 mas of Hanbury Brown, Davis & Allen (1974), MNRAS 167, 121 (the Narrabri intensity interferometer; Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, Table 1, and the JMDC) and the Hipparcos parallax 28.82 +/- 0.11 mas (van Leeuwen 2007, XHIP)

temperature.source: Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, HD 80007: effective temperature 9240 +/- 220 K (Table 6), from the measured angular diameter and the star's flux from the ultraviolet to the infrared

radialVelocity.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331, XHIP, HIP 45238: RV -5.1 +/- 2.3 km/s (quality A)

distance.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry, HIP 45238: the Hipparcos parallax (van Leeuwen 2007) the radius is computed with, 28.82 +/- 0.11 mas, inverted

position.credit: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry

text.card: A subgiant of type A1 IV, 35 parsecs away: 5.9 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 1.59 milliarcseconds, which at its distance is 5.93 solar radii, and its surface is at 9,240 K.
text.locator: Tables 1 and 6, HD 80007: MK type, limb-darkened diameter, effective temperature
